details:
Q1: Isolation is already in place, so what should this re-issue deliver?
Choices:
A) Verification only: add a contract test proving every analysis/retro Codex launch in `workflow-log-analysis.yml` uses `codex_isolated_exec.sh --mode read-only`, then close the finding.
B) A + stop fork-origin runs reaching the agent: in `scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py`, leave out (or mark untrusted) runs whose head repository differs from the repository they ran in, and cover it with tests. (RECOMMENDED)
C) B + move the GitHub-writing steps (issue/comment/commit posting with `GH_TOKEN`) into a separate job that has no model and that consumes the report as an artifact. **Note:** this restructures a very large workflow and may run into the 480,000-byte workflow size guard (§24), which would mean moving inline step bodies into `scripts/` in the same PR.
Q2: If fork-origin filtering is in scope (Q1 B or C), what should happen to fork-origin CI runs?
Choices:
A) Drop them from log selection and full-log export entirely, keep only aggregate counts (run counts and conclusions, no log text), and log each exclusion. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Keep their logs but label them as untrusted fork-origin content in the prompt and the run-logs directory.
C) Drop all `pull_request`-event runs, fork or not.
